key_insight: Nitrogen vacancies locally weaken polar-axis lattice coupling in wurtzite AlN, enabling defect-mediated switching whose spatial distribution and timing determine reversed-domain growth.
engineering_relevance: Controlling nitrogen vacancies, including through scandium doping, offers a route to lower coercive fields for low-voltage ferroelectric memory.
evidence_signal: The combined analysis links vacancy-mediated nucleation to domain-growth behavior and finds that scandium promotes vacancy formation and lowers the coercive field; the abstract reports no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Reliable device implementation requires control of vacancy distributions; switching endurance and leakage trade-offs are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Nitrogen vacancy cluster-mediated ferroelectric domain growth in wurtzite AlN
